citations.claim: initial total momentum is exactly zero at rest
body 1 gains large velocity in one step
total momentum becomes nonzero at first violating step

counterfactual.change: lowered G from 4.013 to 0.5 only; weaker pairwise forces shrink absolute momentum error below tolerance so momentum_conserved passes

explanation: With all bodies initially at rest, one leapfrog step should keep total momentum zero if pairwise forces are equal-and-opposite. Instead momentum jumps to 0.00779. The dv of body 1 (-0.0648,0.0432) scaled by m=1 does not cancel dv of body 2 scaled by m=14.95 (acceleration ratio ~16.8 vs mass ratio 14.96), so the 1-2 force is not antisymmetric. Likely cause is asymmetric force evaluation (e.g. per-body softening or ordering-dependent computation).
vision_note: Both frames look nearly identical with three blue dots holding their positions and no clear motion. There is no obvious collision, ejection, or red-highlighted violating body in step 1.
